rules.action: Pre-dilate with semi-compliant balloon sized 1:1 to RVD. Confirm full expansion before stent delivery. Direct stenting is a reasonable alternative for simple, non-calcified lesions.

Scoring or cutting balloon first-line for focal calcium. Escalate to IVL if residual waist persists after scoring. Cutting balloon preferred for proximal/aorto-ostial straight segments; scoring balloon for tortuous segments.
Scoring or cutting balloon first; escalate to IVL before stenting if waist persists — do not proceed with persistent non-compliance in long lesions.
Plan calcium modification before the case. Intravascular imaging (IVUS/OCT) before selecting modification device. Confirm full balloon compliance before stenting.

IVL for deep/medial calcium, calcified nodules, large vessels, and bifurcation lesions (wire protection possible). RA for superficial calcium, balloon-uncrossable lesions, and small vessels (<2.5mm). OA as RA alternative in experienced centres.

Rotational atherectomy: burr-to-vessel ratio 0.5–0.7; speed 140,000–180,000 rpm; short passes (<30s) with adequate flushing. Limited debulking strategy — goal is to facilitate balloon expansion, not lumen enlargement.
RA followed by IVL (Dual-Prep) is a reasonable escalation when post-atherectomy imaging reveals persistent heavy calcification.
Plan calcium modification before the case. Short RA bursts (<30s) with adequate flushing. Consider staged debulking if diffuse. IVL may require multiple balloons for long segments.
IVL preferred over RA at the ostium. Disengage guide during IVL pulses to avoid aortic root energy transmission.
rules.caution: Do not inflate IVL balloon with guide deeply engaged at the ostium.

rules.action: If balloon won't cross: attempt Rotawire/microcatheter → RA with small burr (1.25mm). If Rotawire also won't cross: consider excimer laser atherectomy. Do not force devices through uncrossable calcium.
Use short marker-to-marker stent. Disengage guide 1–2mm before final deployment. Post-dilate with NC balloon flared at the ostium.
Plan stent overlap zones before deploying. Deploy distal stent first, work proximally. Post-dilate each segment before deploying the next.
rules.caution: Avoid geographic miss at proximal or distal edges — high risk of edge restenosis.

rules.action: Intravascular imaging mandatory before stenting. Deploy stents distal to proximal with ≥3mm overlap zones. Post-dilate each segment before deploying the next.
Routine manual aspiration thrombectomy is NOT recommended during primary PCI. No mortality or reinfarction benefit demonstrated; risk of stroke.
Selective/bailout aspiration thrombectomy may be considered for very large residual thrombus burden after wire/balloon passage when flow remains severely impaired.
Restore antegrade flow before stenting where possible. Staged approach (small balloon → reassess → definitive stenting) reduces no-reflow risk.

IV or intracoronary GP IIb/IIIa inhibitor is reasonable for large thrombus burden, no-reflow, or slow flow during PCI. Intracoronary vasodilators (adenosine, verapamil, nitroprusside) as adjunct for no-reflow.
rules.caution: Routine GP IIb/IIIa administration before angiography is NOT recommended (Class III Harm).

rules.action: Deferred stenting (24–48h with anticoagulation) may be considered when large thrombus persists after flow restoration, to allow thrombus resolution before definitive treatment.
Visible thrombus with preserved flow: avoid routine aspiration. Consider GPI infusion and definitive stenting. If high residual burden persists, deferred stenting (24–48h) is an option.
Avoid aspiration thrombectomy in SVG. EPD mandatory. Consider pharmacoinvasive approach (GP IIb/IIIa) before definitive stenting. Direct stenting preferred over pre-dilation.
rules.caution: Aspiration in a thrombosed degenerated SVG carries high no-reflow risk.

rules.action: Avoid aspiration thrombectomy. EPD as standard. Pre-treat with GP IIb/IIIa. Direct stenting preferred over pre-dilation where anatomy permits.
Direct stenting preferred. Avoid routine pre-dilation unless severely stenotic or EPD delivery requires it. Slow nominal-pressure inflations.
Calcium modification required despite graft setting. IVL preferred over RA in SVG (lower perforation risk). Deploy EPD before calcium modification. Liberal intracoronary vasodilators throughout.
rules.caution: Graft perforation risk is higher than native vessel — use conservative burr sizing if RA is selected.

rules.action: EPD whenever technically feasible (ACC/AHA Class I/B; ESC Class IIa/B). Intracoronary vasodilators (verapamil, adenosine, nitroprusside) liberally — delivered distally via microcatheter or OTW balloon.
Restore flow cautiously. Avoid aspiration thrombectomy in SVG. Deploy EPD first; consider GP IIb/IIIa infusion to reduce thrombus burden. Reassess true lesion severity after flow restoration.
For moderate thrombus: guide extension aspiration. For very large thrombus: mechanical thrombectomy (AngioJet, Penumbra). Maintain high ACT throughout.
rules.caution: Limited RCT evidence for SVG thrombectomy devices.

rules.action: Keep atherectomy bursts and balloon inflations short (<30s). Vasopressors immediately available. Consider staged procedure if haemodynamic reserve is borderline.
Keep inflation times short; deflate promptly if haemodynamics deteriorate. Staged procedure is a reasonable strategy for high-complexity lesions.
Calcium modification must achieve full lesion compliance before stenting. Accept a longer procedure — do not rush preparation.
rules.caution: Do not stent until full balloon compliance is confirmed — no bailout exists if the result is inadequate.

rules.action: IVUS-guided sizing mandatory. Pre-dilate cautiously with vasopressors available. For LM shaft/ostial disease without bifurcation, single stent preferred. Ensure continuous haemodynamic monitoring.
